name: pdk-karapace-rest-proxy-shared-consumer-instances
instr:
# Shared REST consumer instances

We need to put three Kafka REST proxy nodes behind one load balancer without pinning a consumer client to a particular node. Extend the existing v2 consumer API so an instance created on one node can be used from any node.

- Keep the existing `/consumers/{group}` creation response (`instance_id`, `base_uri`) and the node-independent `rest_base_uri` URL, with the current one-node behavior.
- Subscription, assignment lookup, fetch, committed offsets, position changes and commits through any node operate on the same instance. Fetch records retain their Kafka order and current v2 JSON response shape.
- If an owner dies, another node serves the same instance within 45 seconds. Fetch resumes from the Kafka group’s last committed offset; uncommitted records may repeat, but committed records cannot recur and no records may be skipped.
- If an owner is paused, another node can take over and serve its instance within 35 seconds. When the former owner resumes, it cannot serve stale fetches or commits. A request through it can reach the current owner instead.
- DELETE from any node invalidates the instance everywhere; subsequent instance requests return 404, and the same name can then be created again. An idle instance also expires cluster-wide when `consumer_idle_disconnect_timeout` is positive.
- Simultaneous creates of the same name and group on different nodes yield one success and one 409.

Kafka and Redis are available as `kafka:9092` and `redis:6
